q.t: A line that divides a shape into two halves that match exactly when folded is called:
q.e: If you fold along it and the two halves sit exactly on top of each other, the fold is a line of symmetry.

q.t: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
q.e: You can fold a square in half 4 ways: across, up-down, and along both corner-to-corner lines.

q.t: How many lines of symmetry does a rectangle (that is not a square) have?
q.e: Only the across and up-down folds work; a corner-to-corner fold does not match up.

q.t: Which capital letter has a line of symmetry?
q.e: A standing line down the middle of A gives two matching halves.

q.t: How many lines of symmetry does a circle have?
o: Very many — any line through the centre
q.e: Every fold through the centre of a circle makes two matching halves.

q.t: Where is the line of symmetry of a butterfly?
o: Down the middle of its body
q.e: The left wings match the right wings, so the line runs down the body.

q.t: How many lines of symmetry does a triangle with all three sides equal have?
q.e: You can fold from each corner to the middle of the opposite side — 3 ways.

q.t: A paper is folded once and one hole is punched (not on the fold). How many holes do you see when you open it?
q.e: The punch goes through 2 layers of paper, so it makes 2 holes, one on each side of the fold.

q.t: Which tiles can cover a floor with no gaps?
q.e: Squares fit edge to edge; curved tiles always leave gaps between them.

q.t: A mirror is placed along the line of symmetry of half a picture. What do you see?
q.e: The mirror shows the other half exactly, because the two halves of a symmetrical picture match.

q.t: How many lines of symmetry does a regular hexagon (6 equal sides) have?
q.e: 3 lines join opposite corners and 3 join the middles of opposite sides.

q.t: A square paper is folded twice (into quarters) and one hole is punched away from the folds. How many holes appear when opened?
q.e: Two folds make 4 layers, and the punch goes through all of them.

q.t: Which capital letter has NO line of symmetry?
q.e: F has arms only on one side, so no fold makes it match; H, O and X each have lines of symmetry.

q.t: Which word looks exactly the same in a mirror stood upright beside it?
q.e: W and O each have a standing line of symmetry, and WOW reads the same backwards.

q.t: Why is AMBULANCE written back to front on the front of an ambulance?
o: So drivers in front can read it in their mirrors
So people inside can read it
q.e: A mirror flips writing left to right, so back-to-front writing shows the right way round in a mirror.

q.t: How many lines of symmetry does a regular pentagon (5 equal sides) have?
q.e: You can fold from each of the 5 corners to the middle of the opposite side.

q.t: Which digit has a standing (up-down) line of symmetry?
q.e: The left half of 8 matches its right half; 2, 4 and 7 do not.

q.t: A triangle has exactly two equal sides. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
q.e: Only the fold from the top corner, between the two equal sides, makes the halves match.

q.t: How many lines of symmetry does the capital letter H have?
q.e: H matches when folded up-down (left and right) and also across the middle (top and bottom).

q.t: Which shape will NOT tile a floor without gaps?
q.e: Circles touch only at points, leaving curved gaps between them.

q.t: How many lines of symmetry do a square and a rectangle (not a square) have together?
q.e: A square has 4 and a rectangle has 2.

q.t: Which capital letter has BOTH a standing and a sleeping line of symmetry?
q.e: H matches left–right and top–bottom; A and T only left–right; E only top–bottom.

q.t: A square paper is folded twice. A small corner is cut off at the point where both folds meet. How many holes appear when you open it?
q.e: The point where both folds meet is the centre of the paper, so the four cut pieces join into one hole in the middle.

q.t: Which number looks the same in a mirror stood upright beside it?
q.e: 1 and 8 each have a standing line of symmetry, and 181 reads the same backwards.

q.t: How many lines of symmetry do a regular hexagon and an equal-sided triangle have together?
q.e: A regular hexagon has 6 and an equal-sided triangle has 3.

q.t: When we make a floor pattern with tiles, the tiles must have:
o: Overlaps on top of each other
q.e: A good tiling covers every bit of the floor exactly once.

q.t: A paper is folded in half and half a heart is cut along the fold. What do you get when you open it?
o: A whole heart, with the fold as its line of symmetry
q.e: The cut goes through both layers, so the missing half is cut too, joined at the fold.

q.t: Which capital letter has exactly ONE line of symmetry?
q.e: A has only a standing line; H and X have 2, and O has 2 or more.

q.t: How many lines of symmetry does a regular octagon (8 equal sides) have?
q.e: A regular shape has as many lines of symmetry as it has sides: half go corner to corner, half go side-middle to side-middle.

q.t: Which capital letter has ONLY a sleeping (across) line of symmetry?
q.e: B’s top half matches its bottom half, but its left and right are different.

q.t: Which word, written in capital letters, looks the same in a mirror placed below it?
q.e: B, O and X each have a sleeping line of symmetry, so every letter flips onto itself.

q.t: A square paper is folded twice and 2 holes are punched away from the folds. How many holes appear when opened?
q.e: Two folds make 4 layers, and each punch makes 4 holes: 2 × 4.

q.t: A paper is folded in half three times, and one hole is punched through all the layers. How many holes appear when opened?
q.e: Each fold doubles the layers: 2, then 4, then 8.

q.t: A row of tiles repeats red, blue, green, red, blue, green… What colour is the 20th tile?
q.e: The pattern repeats every 3 tiles; 18 tiles make 6 full repeats, so tile 19 is red and tile 20 is blue.

q.t: A pattern repeats square, triangle, triangle, circle. How many triangles are in the first 20 shapes?
q.e: Each group of 4 shapes has 2 triangles, and 20 shapes are 5 groups: 5 × 2 = 10.

q.t: Which 4-digit number looks the same in a mirror stood upright beside it?
q.e: 1881 reads the same backwards and uses only 1 and 8, which have standing lines of symmetry.

q.t: How many letters of the word MATH have a standing (up-down) line of symmetry?
q.e: M, A, T and H can each be folded down the middle into matching halves.

q.t: A shape has 4 equal sides but no right angles (a diamond — like a square pushed over). How many lines of symmetry does it have?
q.e: It folds along both corner-to-corner lines, but not across the middle as a square would.

q.t: A square tile is cut along ALL of its lines of symmetry. How many pieces do you get?
q.e: The 4 lines all pass through the centre and split the square into 8 equal triangles.

q.t: A paper strip is 6 cm long and 4 cm wide. It is folded in half along a line of symmetry so that its two short ends meet. How long is the folded strip (in cm)?
q.e: Folding the short ends together halves the length: 6 ÷ 2.
